summary: Remote-shell daemon driven by WebRTC peer via publisher-mismatched signaling relay, shipped as V8 bytecode
details: Package installs a headless daemon whose entire logic ships as V8 bytecode in dist/bundle.jsc (~5.9 MB), loaded through bytenode.require from bin/vanexa-agent.js with no source available. The daemon receives natural-language commands over a WebRTC DataChannel from a remote peer and executes arbitrary terminal commands, file read/write/edit operations, and full git operations on the installer's host. Peer pairing is bootstrapped through a hardcoded signaling relay at vanexa-agent-relay.tubefood.workers.dev (a Cloudflare Workers subdomain on an unrelated 'tubefood' account) with fallback vanexa-agent-relay.workers.dev, while the publisher identity is @vanexalabs-ai; whoever controls that signaling endpoint controls which peers can pair and drive the command channel. The tarball also ships socket.yml / socket.json that instruct Socket.dev to ignore aiMalware, gptMalware, obfuscatedCode, usesEval, shellAccess, filesystemAccess, networkAccess, bypassesEnvironment, installScripts, and typosquat findings, suppressing audit of the very sinks the bytecode reaches. Network-to-shell dispatch on the installer's host, combined with an opaque bytecode payload and scanner-suppression manifest, is a remote backdoor regardless of the advertised 'phone-driven agent' framing.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
